from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
p=Path('tmp/pdfs'); p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
texts=[]
for i, page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 t=page.extract_text()
 texts.append(f'\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n{t}')
 (p/f'page-{i:02}.txt').write_text(t)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(texts))
print('\\n'.join(texts[:3]))
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses an important efficiency bottleneck in multimodal models. Combining class-attention outlier selection with key-based token merging at the vision–language interface is simple, modular, and potentially useful without architectural changes to the language model.

PruMerge+ demonstrates a meaningful accuracy–token tradeoff. At 25% token retention, the 7B model achieves 76.8 versus 78.5 on VQAv2, 57.1 versus 58.2 on TextVQA, and 64.9 versus 64.3 on MMBench. Such compression can be valuable despite some accuracy loss.

The evaluation includes six image benchmarks, two language-model sizes, and three video benchmarks. Training-free transfer to Video-LLaVA is encouraging, particularly the ActivityNet-QA improvement from 45.3 to 48.3 with PruMerge.

Tables 4–6 provide useful sampling, merging, and fine-tuning ablations. For example, adding token supplementation improves MME from 1221.6 to 1350.3. The figures communicate the main pipeline effectively, and the underlying models, datasets, and related methods are cited.
weaknesses: The principal comparisons do not sufficiently isolate the contribution. PruMerge+ results in Table 7 match the fine-tuned results, but equivalent fine-tuning and implementation conditions for ToMe, ATS, and EViT are not specified; CrossGet numbers are imported from its paper. Additionally, no comparison against fixed top-k attention selection with identical merging and matched average token budgets establishes the benefit of the central IQR-based adaptivity.

The efficiency evidence is exclusively analytical. Table 2 explicitly reports roofline estimates rather than measured runtime or memory. It does not establish end-to-end gains including token-reduction overhead, decoding, and variable-length batching. Its approximately 40-token scenario also does not directly quantify efficiency for the 25%-retention PruMerge+ configuration that provides the strongest accuracy preservation.

The claimed O(n) merging complexity in Section 2.2 is unsupported by the specified algorithm. Computing the full key-similarity matrix in Equation 4 costs O(n²d); even computing similarities only for m selected centers costs O(mnd), which remains quadratic when m scales with n. This undermines the asserted asymptotic advantage over CrossGet, although reducing downstream LLM computation remains plausible.

Algorithm 1 leaves consequential reproducibility ambiguities. PruMerge+ adds m spatial tokens to m selected tokens, which does not explain the reported increase from 5.5% to 25% retention, and its subsequent loop and output still reference only m tokens. The merging equation uses an unnormalized sum and excludes the center from neighbor selection, despite the description of weighted averaging and supplementation. The neighborhood size k and attention-head aggregation are also unspecified.

Performance-preservation claims exceed the evidence for aggressive compression. In Table 1, 7B PruMerge reduces VQAv2 from 78.5 to 72.0, POPE from 85.9 to 76.3, and MME from 1510.7 to 1350.3 despite fine-tuning. Section 4.1 also claims improved POPE performance, contrary to the table. These results can support a useful compression tradeoff, but not the repeated claim of preserving performance without sacrifice.
